notable_absence.finding: The Plan Parameters schema documents indexPartitions, numReplicas, and the deprecated maxPartitionsPerPIndex with real descriptions, but two of its six fields carry no description at all beyond a type and nullability flag: 'hierarchyRules | **Nullable:** yes | String' and 'nodePlanParams | **Nullable:** yes | String'. Both fields appear populated with opaque string values in the example request bodies ('hierarchyRules' : 'hierarchyRules', 'nodePlanParams' : 'nodePlanParams' - literally the field name as a placeholder value, unlike every other field's realistic example), so the Swagger generator has never had real example data to draw from either. A reader cannot learn what either field does from this page.

cross_component_finding: Three findings worth flagging together. (1) A genuine security-tier asymmetry the page states but never explains: 'Query a Search Index' and 'Query a Search Index (Scoped)' both require the Manage security tier (`fts!manage`), not Read (`fts!read`) - the same tier required for creating, updating, and deleting the index definition itself - while 'Get Document Count for an Index' requires only the Statistics tier and 'Get Index Definition' requires only Read. Running a search query is therefore gated as a write-level operation on this REST surface, unlike the Read-gated equivalent on the Web Console/simple-search-rest-api task pages from earlier rounds (role:fts-admin OR role:fts-searcher, both Read-tier there). (2) This page's own formal 'Query Response' schema model declares only `{status: String, results: Object array}` - no hits/took/total_hits/max_score fields at all - while its own worked examples two sections earlier show the full envelope (`status` as an object with total/failed/successful, `hits` array, `total_hits`, `cost`, `max_score`, `took`). This independently reproduces, on a second page, the exact schema-thinness this round's sibling fts-rest-advanced/index.json already flagged for its own pindex-query endpoint's identically-shaped bare {status, results} response - suggesting the underlying cb-swagger spec's QueryResponse model definition is generated thin everywhere it is reused, not a one-off omission. (3) This page names four concrete internal permission strings tied to named roles (`cluster.bucket[$BUCKET_NAME].fts!manage`/`fts!write`/`fts!read`/`stats!read`, each mapped to Search Admin or Search Reader) - a second, sharper counter-example to the registry's `hasPrivilege` finding that 'Server's docs define a privilege tier... and then never name a member of it' (see role:fts-admin's collision note and round 21's appendix_5_python.md partial counter-example, which names only one permission string). This page names four, systematically, for one service - the strongest concrete-permission evidence found so far for Search specifically.
cross_product_finding: Not applicable - per this round's framing, no Capella twin exists for any fts-rest-* page. This page's REST surface (index CRUD, ingest/freeze/query control, per-index stats, index-scoped querying) is also structurally distinct from the older server/7.2/search/create-search-index-rest-api.md task page (a curl walkthrough for a single PUT operation): that page never mentions ingestControl, planFreezeControl, queryControl, analyzeDoc, pindexLookup, or the scoped-vs-legacy endpoint split, so it is not treated as a twin - this page is a first-contact, comprehensive reference for a surface the task page only sampled one corner of.
